bio: Entry no. 1187 in al-Mizzi's Tahdhib al-Kamal (continued on shamela.ws/book/3722/2679): Hassan ibn Bilal al-Muzani al-Basri, cited by al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah. He narrated from the Companions Hakim ibn Hizam, Ammar ibn Yasir, Yazid ibn Qatada al-Anazi and an unnamed Companion of Aslam; those who narrated from him include Abu Bishr Ja'far ibn Abi Wahshiyya, Abu Qilaba al-Jarmi, Qatada, Matar al-Warraq and Yahya ibn Abi Kathir. Ali ibn al-Madini called him thiqa; the editor's notes add that Ibn Hibban and al-Dhahabi deemed him reliable and Ibn Hajar graded him saduq. No death year is given.

bio: Entry no. 3574 in Tahdhib al-Kamal (al-Mizzi) on shamela.ws: 'Abd al-Malik bin Ya'la al-Laythi al-Basri, judge (qadi) of Basra. He narrated in mursal form from the Prophet, and from 'Imran ibn Husayn, his father Ya'la al-Laythi, and a man of his people. Among those who narrated from him are Aban al-Sarimi, Iyas bin Mu'awiya, Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani, Qatada bin Di'ama and Yunus bin 'Ubayd. Ibn Hibban listed him in al-Thiqat and stated he died in the year 100 AH. The entry notes disagreement over whether he died in office as judge or was removed by Khalid al-Qasri, who appointed Thumama in his place. His hadith is cited by al-Bukhari in ta'liq form (siglum خت).

bio: Tahdhib al-Kamal (al-Mizzi; entry continues on shamela.ws/book/3722/14922) records Muslim bin Kaysan al-Dabbi al-Mula'i, Abu 'Abdullah al-Kufi, known as Muslim al-A'war (the one-eyed). He narrated from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Anas bin Malik, Habba al-'Urani, Sa'id bin Jubayr and his father Kaysan al-Dabbi; those who narrated from him include Isra'il bin Yunus, Ayyub bin Jabir, Jarir bin 'Abd al-Hamid al-Dabbi, al-Hasan bin Salih and Shu'ba bin al-Hajjaj. bio: Ziyad bin Jariya al-Tamimi al-Dimashqi (also called Zayd or Yazid) is a Damascene narrator with 61 recorded narrations; he is said to have had companionship with the Prophet, and his death is placed in the time of al-Walid bin 'Abd al-Malik, between 91 and 100 AH. He narrated from 'Umar bin al-Khattab and Habib bin Maslama al-Fihri, and Makhul, Sulayman bin Musa al-Ashdaq and 'Atiyya bin Qays al-Kilabi are among those who narrated from him. Of sixteen critical assessments, several count him among the companions, two grade him trustworthy and Ibn Hibban listed him in al-Thiqat, while some call him an unknown shaykh. His narrations appear in Sunan Abi Dawud, Ibn Majah and Musnad Ahmad.

bio: Wikipedia describes al-Husayn ibn Numayr al-Sakuni as a leading general of the early Umayyad Caliphate from the Sakun subtribe of Kinda. He served as governor of Jund Hims (680-683) under Yazid I, fought at Siffin (657) and al-Harra (683), and led the two-month siege of Ibn al-Zubayr in Mecca in 683 during which the Kaaba burned. He defeated the Penitents at 'Ayn al-Warda (685) and was killed at the Battle of Khazir alongside 'Ubayd Allah ibn Ziyad on 5 or 6 August 686. The page does not give a Hijri death year or discuss hadith narration.
research_evidence: Al-Ḥuṣayn ibn Numayr al-Sakūnī (died 5/6 August 686) was a leading general of the early Umayyad Caliphate, from the Sakun subtribe of the Kinda.

bio: Tahdhib al-Kamal (al-Mizzi, entry 1870) lists al-Rabi' bin Muhammad, counted among the Successors (tabi'un). He narrated in mursal form from the Prophet that he said the takbir; Yahya bin Abi Kathir narrated from him.
